memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Remember that you were slaves in Egypt. That is why I command you to do this. - Deut 24:22 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The chapter closes with a simple but powerful reminder, "Remember that you were slaves in Egypt." This is the reason behind all the commands for generosity and justice toward the vulnerable. God's people were to let the memory of their own bondage, and of God's gracious rescue, shape how they treated others. Because they had been helpless and God had shown them mercy, they were to show mercy in turn.

This is one of the great motivations for compassion in all of Scripture, remembering what God has done for us. Israel's ethics were rooted not in cold duty but in grateful memory. They had experienced slavery and then astonishing deliverance. That memory was meant to soften their hearts and open their hands toward everyone in need around them.

For us, this points straight to the gospel. We were slaves too, not in Egypt, but to sin, and we could not free ourselves. Then God, in His great mercy, redeemed us through the blood of His Son, bringing us out of darkness into His marvellous light (1 Pet 2:9-10). Remembering our own rescue is the deepest fuel for a generous, compassionate, justice-loving life. When we forget what God has done, we grow hard and selfish; when we remember, our hearts open. As you recall your own redemption in Christ, how does that memory move you to greater love and generosity toward others?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. How does remembering your redemption change your heart?
2. Where has forgetting God's mercy made you selfish?
3. How can gratitude fuel greater love for others?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You for rescuing me from slavery to sin through Christ. Let the memory of Your mercy make me generous, compassionate, and just. Amen.
